clue.text: From women's side, one way to cut a flower

indicators.note: one piece is said to cut into the other, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: a daff is an informal name for a daffodil
the Roman numeral one is I
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A gardener's tip, apparently, on how best to cut a flower, credited to the women of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the distaff side' means on the mother's side of a family, the distaff being the spinning stick once tied to women's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side of a family is the female line, so the word works as an adjective meaning maternal.

clue.text: Play at bones, risking becoming them?

definitions.text: Play at bones, risking becoming them?

parts.words: Play at bones, risking becoming them?
parts.note: bones are slang for dice, and one who gambles with life may end up a skeleton

explanation.surface: Gambling with dice while courting the danger of ending up as a skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a big risk with one's life is the idiom, with dice called bones in slang.

clue.text: Lilac no good planted in troubled country

indicators.note: the letters are planted inside the other word, as in a garden bed

parts.note: Syria, a country beset by civil war

explanation.surface: A useless plant has been put in the ground in a war-torn land.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the botanical genus name of the lilac shrub.

clue.text: Examples thus introduced in different ways for analysis

parts.note: examples are introduced with as, in phrases like cities such as Rome
another way to introduce an example is with say, as in a city, say Rome

explanation.surface: A writing tip: vary how you introduce examples when presenting analysis.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words introduce an example, two different ways of doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test of a metal or ore to determine its composition, a chemical analysis.

clue.text: The joy of bustling city life

indicators.note: bustling suggests busy movement, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Praise for the pleasures of busy urban living.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is happiness or bliss, a synonym of joy.

clue.text: As artist, live amid works

indicators.note: amid places one piece in the middle of the other

parts.note: a machine that works runs
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to live as an artist, surrounded by their own works.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Paul Rubens was the Flemish Baroque painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubens is an example of a painter, one of the great Flemish masters.

clue.text: Take for granted missing page in summary

indicators.note: missing means a letter is left out

parts.note: to presume is to assume or take for granted

explanation.surface: Someone takes it for granted that a page is missing from a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is a brief account or précis of something.

clue.text: Plates, etc, almost hold together Aussie creature that's died out

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: to bond is to hold together

indicators.note: out means the letter for died is taken out

parts.note: the echidna is a spiny anteater of Australia
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Plates and dishes might nearly cling to an Australian animal that is extinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims BOND to BON; 'died out' removes D from ECHIDNA to give ECHINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates, cups and dishes are typical items made of this fine porcelain containing bone ash.

clue.text: American programme that won't employ old hands?

definitions.meaning: Roosevelt's 1930s economic recovery programme in the USA
in card games a fresh deal gives new hands, not old ones

explanation.surface: A US jobs scheme that refuses to hire experienced workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hands' looks like veteran workers, but means hands of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Deal was Franklin Roosevelt's programme of reforms; a fresh deal of cards gives new hands.

clue.text: Potential skipper, originally simply human, scarily changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the gathered letters take a new order
originally points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A description of someone being transformed, simply and frighteningly, from a human into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: S and H, the initials of 'simply' and 'human', join SCARILY and 'changed' rearranges all nine. A skipper is a small butterfly, so the pupa is a skipper in the making.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa is the stage before a butterfly such as a skipper emerges, so it is a skipper in potential.

clue.text: One welcomes receiving post

indicators.note: the two words receive, or hold within them, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: Someone who welcomes visitors is also the one who takes in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like letters, but it is an upright: a newel is the post at the foot of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the main upright at the end of a stair's handrail, a kind of post.

clue.text: One way to finger extremists?

parts.note: read FRINGE with lunatic as an anagram signal: a crazy arrangement of fringe gives finger

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how to point out radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is wordplay itself: an anagram of the second word, signalled by the first, makes 'finger'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fringe of any movement holding wild views is its most extreme wing.

clue.text: Not quite straight as a policy adviser?

definitions.meaning: a wonk is a policy expert, so playfully the word is read as being like a wonk

explanation.surface: Is a policy adviser ever entirely straight with us?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a joke: a policy wonk, plus the adjective ending -y.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lopsided or unsteady is described as crooked, slightly off true.

clue.text: One that won't fight spy making one change and confess

parts.note: CO stands for conscientious objector, someone who refuses to fight

indicators.note: one letter of the spy's name is swapped for another

parts.note: Donald Maclean was one of the Cambridge spies who passed secrets to Moscow

explanation.surface: A pacifist turned spy has a change of heart and owns up.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the A of MACLEAN for an E to get MECLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up fully and tell the truth is an idiom for admitting everything.

clue.text: In bits, still about to hold that function

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it
about tells us the word for still is turned round

parts.note: still, as in even now, is yet
something in bits has come apart

explanation.surface: Someone, still in pieces, is about to host the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns YET into TEY, which holds APART.
explanation.definitionFit: A function is a social gathering, and an afternoon party with tea is one such gathering.

clue.text: On a charge, drunk in port

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sailor arrested for drunkenness in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine, which fits 'drunk', but it is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is a harbour city in Alaska, and an anchorage is any place ships may moor.

clue.text: A boring cocktail?

parts.note: the name belongs both to a small hand tool for boring holes and to a drink of gin and lime

explanation.surface: A dull drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hand drill and a gin and lime drink, hence a drink that bores.

clue.text: I'm starting, say, to intrude on stars

indicators.note: one piece intrudes into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: stars of a story are its heroes
EG, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Someone about to barge in on celebrities announces their move.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone says on beginning something risky.

clue.text: Flaw in diamonds: result, one female's off

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

indicators.note: one of the letters is off, taken away

parts.note: a result is an effect
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A jeweller finds a flaw in diamonds, and the upshot is that one woman leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaw is a fault or imperfection in something.

clue.text: Didn't manage to cross line, so beaten

indicators.note: the outer word crosses through the line, holding it

parts.note: to fail is to not manage

explanation.surface: A runner couldn't get over the finishing line and so was defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Flailed can mean thrashed, as with a flail used to beat grain.

clue.text: Particular poet's last to come to the fore in film

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pic is an informal word for a film

indicators.text: 's last to come to the fore
indicators.note: the poet's final letter moves round to the front

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A fussy note about a poet's final line being brought forward in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving Dante's last letter to the front gives EDANT, which goes into PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular can mean fussy and exacting, the same as overly precise about details.

clue.text: Here one must change skirt after only half a season

indicators.note: after means the skirt comes after the half season
only the back half of the season's name is used

parts.note: winter is a season
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A fashion rule: switch skirts once half the season has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: TER is the last half of WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end stations, where passengers must change trains or buses.

clue.text: Sticker may be mine

definitions.meaning: a shellfish that clings tightly to rocks
a ... mine is a magnetic explosive stuck to a ship's hull

explanation.surface: Someone claims a sticker as possibly theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive, but is the explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish clings to rocks, and the naval mine is named for it since it is attached the same way.

clue.text: Take apart an alliance, one near abandoning resistance

parts.note: an indefinite article, here as A
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, a military alliance

indicators.note: the near one abandons a letter, losing it

parts.note: near can mean stingy, and one who is stingy is a miser
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Someone breaks up an alliance because one member is no longer resisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' looks like close, but in old British use it means mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect something is to take it apart, literally or in analysis.

clue.text: Nurse has not enough energy for progress at work

indicators.note: the word is short of one letter

parts.note: a career is one's progress through working life
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A nurse lacks the energy to advance in her job.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who looks after someone who is ill or frail is a nurse in the general sense.

clue.text: Rate at first constant later fell

indicators.note: later puts the second piece after the first
at first takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a fell is an animal's skin or hide

explanation.surface: A reading of a measurement that started steady and then dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' looks like speed, but in old use to rate is to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone, in an old sense, is to berate or scold them.

clue.text: Briefly share a sweet

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to share something equally is to halve it

explanation.surface: An instruction to split a sweet quickly with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Halva is a confection of sesame paste and sugar, a sweet from the Middle East.

clue.text: Supply in condition, I note

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a proviso is a condition in a contract

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the stock being in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: N for note is a convention from rendering notes as single letters; I goes inside PROVISO.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply of something laid in for later is a store or stock.

clue.text: Pounds being invested, that is by no means the best for industry

definitions.text: by no means the best for industry

indicators.note: the pounds are invested, or put inside, the other piece

parts.note: id est, Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.
L, from Latin libra, stands for pounds

explanation.surface: Pounds invested, it seems, do not always go to the best business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'industry' here means hard work, not business.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry means diligence, so the least diligent are the laziest of all.

clue.text: Like a mule to be free of germs

definitions.meaning: a mule cannot breed, being infertile

explanation.surface: A mule apparently aspires to cleanliness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unable to reproduce and clean of microbes, both forms of barrenness.
